## Hands-on 5 – The preregistration {#the-preregistration-moment}

::: {.none}
1. Open the preregistration block of Task 5 in your report
2. Complete fields 1–5: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification, the one-sentence justification from your causal graph, and your rule for what supports or undermines the claim
3. **Render**, or on the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes
4. Type **"declared"** in chat – then wait for the class
:::

::: {.fragment}
Nobody runs a model until everyone in the class has completed their preregistration block.
:::

::: notes
We preregister together, because a thing that the whole class does at once sticks in a way that an instruction does not. Open Task 5. Fill in the five fields: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification with an option for each decision of the menu, the one-sentence justification that your graph gives you, and the rule, written now and before any result, for what would support the claim and what would undermine it. The data-in-hand statement is where you record what you already know about the data before you fix your specification. Render the report; the rendered file with its timestamp is the dated record of your preregistration. Then type "declared" in chat, and wait. [count them in aloud] And if the specification you choose is one that you already tried in Task 4, that is allowed, but say so in the block, because a specification whose result you have already seen is not preregistered in the strict sense.
:::

## Hands-on 5 – The preregistered run {#run-it-then-watch-the-chart .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Task 5** – run the specification in your preregistration, and only that one, with `run_spec()`
- `report_result()` prints a one-click link to the results form with your values already in it – open it, press Send
- Your result joins the **Multiverse** page as a *declared* result, a filled circle beside the open circles of the exploration in Task 4
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Compare the two waves. If the declared results fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, it is worth discussing why.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Stuck? Type "STUCK" · reload and rerun · try a second browser · follow my screen · last resort: your specification is one row of `spec_curve.csv`, with its estimate and its test, and I will help you submit it by hand
:::

::: notes
Go. Run the specification in your preregistration, just that one, with run underscore spec, and when the numbers are in front of you call report underscore result. It prints a link to the results form with your values already filled in: one click, press Send, and you have submitted. Your mark joins the chart as a declared result, a filled circle, beside the open circles that the class submitted in Task 4. If the declared results fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, that tells you something about what people chose to preregister once they had tried the alternatives, and it is worth a conversation. If anything misbehaves, type STUCK and work down the ladder on the cheatsheet. And if your machine is truly finished for the day, your specification is one row of the curve file, with its estimate and its test, and I will help you submit it by hand. Everybody gets a mark on the chart.
:::
